excerpt: A counseling practice scope has to cover quiet session rooms, upholstered furniture, and client restrooms without disturbing clinicians or touching confidential material. This checklist breaks tasks into per-visit, weekly, and monthly tiers and shows which ones push labor hours up.
quickAnswer: A therapy and counseling scope covers per-visit trash and tissue-heavy waste removal in every session room, vacuuming carpet and upholstery edges, restroom disinfection and restocking, and kitchen and waiting room touch points, with weekly upholstery vacuuming and monthly detail work. A 3,600 sq ft group practice with two restrooms typically needs about 1.2 to 1.8 labor hours per visit. Upholstery care, group room resets, quiet-equipment requirements, and confidentiality protocols are what push hours above a standard office.

blocks.text: Scope Principles for a Counseling Practice

A therapy office is built around privacy and calm. Session rooms have sound masking, soft lighting, upholstered seating, rugs, and personal touches from each clinician. Files, notebooks, and laptops may sit on desks. The janitorial scope has to clean all of that without moving clinical materials, without lingering in rooms, and without leaving chemical odors that a client will notice the next morning. A good scope is specific about what the crew touches and what it leaves alone.

Write three rules into the top of the scope. First, crews never open drawers, file cabinets, or folders, and never discard paper other than what is in the trash. Second, crews use fragrance-free or low-VOC products in session rooms. Third, if a clinician leaves a room marked do not clean, the crew skips it and logs the skip. These rules cost almost nothing in labor but prevent the complaints that end contracts.

blocks.text: Those tasks total roughly 102 to 136 minutes, or about 1.7 to 2.3 hours for one cleaner. Two-person crews working efficiently land at about 1.2 to 1.8 total labor hours, slightly more than the ISSA general office benchmark of 3,500 sq ft per hour would suggest for 3,600 sq ft plus two restrooms. The difference comes from the number of small rooms: every door opened, every liner changed, and every lamp switch wiped adds seconds that a cubicle floor does not have.

blocks.title: Session rooms drive the clock
blocks.text: Twelve session rooms at 4 to 5 minutes each consume nearly half of the visit. If a bid estimates under an hour for this practice, ask how many minutes they allot per session room and whether vacuuming is included every visit.

items: Weekly: vacuum upholstered chair and sofa cushions and crevices in session rooms and the waiting room.
Weekly: dust picture frames, window sills, blinds, and bookshelves without moving books or clinician items.
Weekly: clean interior glass on entry doors and the reception window.
Weekly: wipe baseboards in corridors and the group therapy room where chairs scuff walls.
Monthly: detail-vacuum carpet edges and under furniture that can be moved safely.
Monthly: high dust vents, light fixtures, and sound-masking speakers.
Monthly: clean trash receptacles inside and out and disinfect wastebaskets in session rooms.
Quarterly: hot-water carpet extraction in corridors and waiting room, amortized at $0.03 to $0.06 per sq ft per month; upholstery spot cleaning quoted separately.

blocks.text: Turning the Checklist Into a Price

Use your labor estimate as a check against bids. At 1.5 labor hours per visit and $35 to $65 per hour for standard commercial labor, direct labor runs $53 to $98 per visit. After supervision, supplies, insurance, and margin, vendors land around $353 to $599 per visit for a 3,600 sq ft practice with mixed flooring and two restrooms. At three visits per week, that is 13 visits per month using 4.33 weeks, or about $4,600 to $7,800 per month. Twice-weekly service at 8.66 visits brings the range down to roughly $3,100 to $5,200.

items.name: Inventory rooms
items.text: Count session rooms, group rooms, clinician offices, restrooms, and the kitchen. Note flooring for each.

items.name: Set minutes per room
items.text: Use 4 to 5 minutes per session room, 8 to 12 per restroom, and 8 to 12 for the group room as a starting point.

items.name: Amortize weekly and monthly tasks
items.text: Divide each periodic task's minutes by the number of visits in that period and add them to the per-visit total.

items.name: Apply a labor rate
items.text: Standard commercial rates of $35 to $65 per hour fit most practices; behavioral health centers with medical services may need $55 to $95 specialty crews.

items.name: Compare bids line by line
items.text: Ask each bidder for minutes per room and a written list of exclusions.

blocks.text: Tools Matched to Quiet, Carpet-Heavy Spaces

Group rooms and corridors with LVT are faster with a Rubbermaid 36-inch cotton dust mop on a swivel frame with a 60-inch handle, which clears a wide path before damp mopping and makes no noise. For damp mopping, a Rubbermaid HYGEN 18-inch microfiber flat mop with a 2-quart onboard tank needs no bucket, so crews can move quickly between small rooms without carting water. For restrooms, an Unger 15-gallon dual-bucket SmartColor system keeps dirty rinse water separate from clean solution, so restroom soil is not carried onto the kitchen or corridor floors.

blocks.title: Chemicals and HazCom
blocks.text: Even low-hazard practices must have Safety Data Sheets available for every chemical the crew brings on site, under OSHA's Hazard Communication Standard. Ask the vendor to leave an SDS binder or digital link, and confirm restroom disinfectants are EPA-registered.

faqs.q: How long does it take to clean a therapy office?
faqs.a: A 3,600 sq ft practice with 12 session rooms and two restrooms takes about 1.2 to 1.8 labor hours per visit with a two-person crew. A 1,200 sq ft solo or two-clinician suite usually takes 40 to 60 minutes.

faqs.q: Should cleaners move clinician belongings to clean desks?
faqs.a: No. Scope language should say crews clean only clear desk surfaces and never move papers, files, or devices. Clinicians who want desks cleaned should clear them before leaving.

faqs.q: How often should upholstered furniture be cleaned in a counseling practice?
faqs.a: Vacuum cushions and crevices weekly. Spot-clean stains as they appear, and schedule professional upholstery cleaning once or twice a year, which is usually quoted outside the regular contract.

faqs.q: What are common scope exclusions for therapy practices?
faqs.a: Carpet extraction, upholstery shampooing, exterior windows, emptying shred bins, and handling any paper outside trash cans are common exclusions. Make sure exclusions are listed in writing so every bid covers the same work.

faqs.q: Do therapy office crews need special training?
faqs.a: Standard commercial training plus HazCom chemical awareness is enough for most practices. Add confidentiality expectations to onboarding, and require bloodborne pathogens training only if the practice offers injections, lab draws, or medication services.
